subject: Hosted API: intermittent stream quiescence — update & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cortexus.ai>, ops@cortexus.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: intermittent stream quiescence — initial notice

Hi Elena / Cortexus ops team,

Wanted to make you aware of an ongoing intermittent degradation impacting streaming responses from our hosted API in US-West (us-west-1). You may see streams that open successfully but then stop emitting tokens for a 6–20s window before resuming — we’re calling this behavior "stream quiescence." This affects a subset of requests using long-lived sessions and streaming-enabled routes.

What we know so far:
- Onset: ~2028-07-09 08:45 PDT.
- Symptoms: streaming connections remain established, after ~2–40 tokens there can be pauses of 6–20s followed by normal continuation. Non-streaming (batch) requests are not impacted.
- Scope: ~2.5% of streaming requests across a small set of model variants in us-west-1. Not observed in eu or apac.
- Mitigation in progress: we’ve applied a temporary routing change to divert affected traffic to a warmed pool; that has reduced but not eliminated occurrences.

Immediate customer impact: some streaming responses in your flows (chat sessions with long context) may appear to stall briefly. No data loss; resumed tokens are contiguous.

Next steps:
- Our on-call (Marissa) is running targeted trace collection and a KV/cache eviction audit.
- We will publish an incident update and timeline to our status page within the hour.
- ETA for a permanent mitigation: 24–48 hours pending root cause (likely related to an opportunistic kernel selection path interacting with our streaming fanout).

Attachments: sample logs and initial p95 chart included (internal).

We’ll keep this thread for customer-facing updates. If you see any outage beyond the brief stalls please reply and we’ll escalate.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cortexus.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, ops@cortexus.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 09:25:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: intermittent stream quiescence — initial notice

Jonas, thanks for the heads-up.

Quick questions from our side:
1) Is there any observable client-side action we should take (reconnect/backoff) or will behaviour be transparent to clients that keep the stream open?
2) Can you confirm whether our tenant was routed to the warmed pool automatically or if we need to make a ticket to get traffic shifted?

We have a handful of long-running chat sessions (2+ min) used by ops staff — these stalls cause UX confusion; if there’s a workaround we’ll implement it while you triage.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform, Cortexus AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cortexus.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: intermittent stream quiescence — initial notice

Jonas — quick internal summary and recommended customer message:

TL;DR: routing warm-pool diversion reduced incidents from ~2.5% -> ~0.9% for affected model variants. Root cause hypothesis: an interaction between a new kernel selector path (deployed 2028-07-07) and prefetch coalescing under certain tokenization patterns (long prompt prefixes).

Immediate ops actions I have running:
- Continued trace aggregation for affected request IDs (logs attached).
- Roll forward a temporary kernel-selector override on canary nodes (30% traffic) to measure delta.
- Prepare a status page update and a short customer-facing blurb for Cortexus and other affected customers.

Suggested message for Cortexus (to be sent from you, Jonas) — include: what happened, who is affected, observed customer impact, immediate mitigations, ETA for fix, pointer to status page, and a contact for urgent escalation. Keep it short and include the status link.

Lauren — can you review the customer-facing wording quickly and suggest edits?

I’ll keep an eye on canary metrics and will ping you when we have a clear delta.

—
Marissa
Staff Engineer, Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cortexus.ai>, ops@cortexus.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: stream quiescence update — status page entry and next steps

Hi Elena — quick update following today’s triage. Thank you for the quick reply this morning and for flagging the UX impact.

What we published: we’ve posted a short incident on our public status page with current scope and mitigations: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incidents/2028-07-09-stream-quiescence.

What changed since morning:
- Canary kernel-selector override (30% traffic) decreased observed quiescence occurrences from ~0.9% -> ~0.08% over the 4h window.
- We’ve widened the diversion to 60% for affected model variants to reduce customer exposure while we prepare a targeted rollback for the kernel selector change rolled 2028-07-07.
- No data loss or request termination observed; streams resume and tokens continue in-order.

Customer action: None required immediately. If you prefer to be routed off the warmed pool to avoid any transient routing, we can open a tenant-level diversion for Cortexus — that will route your streaming requests to the stable pool until tomorrow’s rollback. Reply to this thread if you want us to activate that for your tenant (it can be done today).

Next steps and timeline:
- Short-term (0–24h): maintain 60% diversion; monitor; offer tenant-level diversion on request.
- Medium-term (24–72h): rollback kernel-selector path from 2028-07-07 on affected clusters and validate in canary.
- Postmortem: draft outline attached; we will share a full postmortem (timeline, root cause, remediation) within 5 working days.

Attachments: sample request logs, p95 trend graphic, PM outline.

If you’d like a quick 15-minute sync to walk through the data and mitigation, I’m available 17:00–18:00 PT today.

Thanks again for your patience — we’ll keep you posted here and on the status page.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Operations: ops@redwood-inference.com
